companyDescription: Earth Observation Satellites · One of the largest commercial Earth-imaging fleets — daily global imaging for government, agriculture, and defense customers
priceNote: Trading $26.51, down 37% from its all-time high just over a month ago (~$51 in early June) despite a genuine Q1 FY27 earnings beat — the market punished the print on continued net losses, negative free cash flow, and a dilutive equity raise rather than the revenue growth itself.
summary: Planet Labs reported record Q1 FY27 revenue of $94M (+42% YoY) on Jun 4, 2026, beating on both revenue and EPS — yet the stock fell and kept falling, now down 37% from its ATH on profit-taking, continued net losses, and a dilutive equity raise. That overreaction has opened a real gap: median analyst target $38 implies ~43% upside from $26.51, with 80% of analysts at Buy or Strong Buy. The Transporter-17 rideshare mission (Jul 8, 2026) already delivered the Pelican-11 tech-demo satellite; the next hard catalyst is Q2 FY27 earnings on Sep 8, where the market will be watching path-to-profitability commentary as closely as growth.

catalysts.name: Q2 FY2027 Earnings
catalysts.description: Next earnings after a Q1 beat that the market still sold off on — this print needs to show either a credible path to profitability or continued net-loss narrowing, not just revenue growth, to reverse the post-earnings de-rating.

risks: The market has now sold off TWICE on genuinely good news (Q1 beat) — shows sentiment is currently anchored to profitability/cash-burn concerns, not growth headlines, so a Sep 8 beat alone may not be enough
Continued net losses and negative free cash flow remain unresolved — the equity raise that triggered part of the selloff signals capital needs that could recur
Down 37% from ATH in just over a month — high realized volatility means position sizing needs to be conservative even with a Buy-heavy analyst base
Small-cap ($5.4B) with thinner analyst coverage (5-10 analysts) than mega-cap semis names — price targets are less consensus-tested and can move more on single-firm revisions
Hawkish Fed dot-plot shift disproportionately hits small/mid-cap growth names with negative FCF, since they're the most duration-sensitive to discount-rate changes
Earth-observation is a competitive, capital-intensive business (Maxar, BlackSky, and government-owned constellations) — pricing power is not guaranteed even with fleet scale

macroRisk.rateOutlook: Fed held 3.50–3.75% for a 4th straight meeting (Jun 17, 2026). Next FOMC Jul 28–29 — CME FedWatch prices ~89% probability of another hold, but the June dot plot raised the median 2026 rate projection, now leaning toward a hike rather than a cut.
macroRisk.inflationNote: Inflation still running above the 2% target; the hawkish dot-plot shift removes a rate-cut tailwind that negative-FCF growth names like PL depend on more than profitable mega-caps.
macroRisk.sectorImpact: Small-cap, negative-free-cash-flow names are the most duration-sensitive to discount-rate assumptions — a hawkish surprise would compress PL's valuation multiple faster than it would a profitable mega-cap, compounding the existing profitability-concern overhang.
macroRisk.summary: MEDIUM-HIGH for this name specifically — the hawkish dot-plot shift is a bigger relative risk for PL than for the profitable mega-caps in this dashboard, given its negative FCF profile.

catalystSpot.preRunup: PL ran up sharply into its Jun 4 print (over 162% YTD coming into June, above $51/share) on momentum — the stock has NOT shown a consistent pre-earnings-runup pattern independent of broader momentum swings, given its short public trading history and small float.

postWin.note: Jun 4, 2026 (Q1 FY27): revenue beat at $94M (+42% YoY) with an EPS beat too, yet shares slipped in after-hours trading and the stock is now down 37% over the following month — the market punished continued net losses and a dilutive equity raise despite the top-line beat. This is the critical nuance for PL: a beat alone does not guarantee a positive reaction here.

postLose.note: No clean recent EPS/revenue miss on record — the closest analog is the post-beat selloff itself (-37% over a month), which functioned like a miss reaction despite beating on paper because guidance/cash-burn concerns dominated the market's read.

spotSizing.reason: Speculative BUY — real 43% median-target upside and a Buy-heavy analyst base, but PL's own history shows beats don't guarantee a positive reaction here, and negative FCF adds real risk. Size at 3% initial, small-cap speculative sizing, add only on confirmed stabilization.

stopPostCatalyst.note: If Sep 8 earnings show no progress on path-to-profitability (net losses widening, another dilutive raise), exit — the market has shown it will punish that even with revenue growth
